purpose: Known gaps of the transitional C backend (issue #27). Each program is valid Core 0.1 that argorixc core-check accepts. The corpus records today's behaviour so a fix is noticed and can be promoted into tests/selfhost/runtime/cases.json.

gaps.note: Array typedefs are emitted sorted by name, so the outer array precedes the inner one.
Struct definitions are emitted alphabetically instead of in dependency order.
The array typedef is emitted before the struct it contains.
A block expression's locals are not wrapped in a C scope.
A unit function whose body ends in a call emits `return <value>;` inside void.
Array types declared inside if/block expressions never get a typedef.
Struct field names reach C unprefixed, so C keywords collide.
Valid Core with an unused parameter fails the declared -Wall -Wextra -Werror profile.
The left operand of a comparison is emitted as a bool temporary; without -Werror this would silently compare 1 < 3.
After the inner scope closes the emitter still treats x as u8, truncating 1000 to 232.
The left operand is read after the right side mutates it, against spec/core/evaluation.md.
`if` used as a statement is not lowered yet.
gaps.signature: if expression needs an expected scalar type

gaps.note: Shifts are defined by the spec (amount below the width, otherwise a trap).
gaps.signature: checked shifts are not implemented yet

gaps.note: Signed negation is defined by the spec and must trap on MIN.
gaps.signature: checked signed negation is not implemented yet

gaps.note: Native stack overflow (SIGSEGV) instead of the typed depth/step trap the spec requires.

An arithmetic expression containing an `if` is rejected when it is a comparison operand: the expected bool type is pushed into the operand (same root cause as g09). Found by the differential generator.
